lens: modern terminal Tetris UX, validated with evidence. First identify the current task from the plan. If it has no user-visible effect, do not invent unrelated UX work. If it creates, changes, or verifies the interface, inspect the relevant renderer and run or capture the terminal output; do not judge from filenames, test counts, or claims in a work log alone. A satisfactory board must render every occupied and active cell as a solid two-character-wide block with ANSI foreground or background colour, preserve a clear cell grid and board boundary, and use recognisably different colours for tetrominoes. Outline-only or monochrome placeholders such as [], {}, XX, or an unfilled glyph are blocking failures. Require readable contrast, an obvious active piece and settled stack, visible score, concise controls, a prominent game-over state, stable redraw without scrolling or cursor debris, and the complete display within the seed's 24-row limit. Inspect automated checks that demonstrate filled cells, ANSI colour, layout bounds, and game-over presentation; run the relevant checks when possible. Put only concrete failures of the current task in findings. Suggestions and optional polish are not findings. Return satisfied true with an empty findings array only when the inspected code and output provide evidence for every applicable requirement.
